final_prompt:
Our product currently has no concept of a team workspace, and we want to add one. The PRD you write will be the shared reference that product, design, and engineering use to scope the work, so it has to be specific enough to estimate from. You're writing a document only, so don't change any code.

Before writing, read the repo so the PRD matches what exists. Look at the README, the docs folder, and the code for accounts, auth, permissions, and billing. Limit the search to those areas. Note how users, ownership of data, and sharing work today. Then use the AskUserQuestion tool to interview me, a few questions at a time, on whatever the repo can't answer. Cover at least these:
- who the workspaces are for
- how members are invited and removed
- roles and permissions
- which existing data becomes workspace-owned
- how billing changes
- how existing individual accounts migrate
- what is explicitly out of scope for the first release

If I don't know an answer, propose a default, mark it as an assumption, and move on.

Then write the PRD to docs/prd-team-workspaces.md. Create no other files. Use these sections:
1. Problem and motivation
2. Goals and non-goals
3. Users and key scenarios
4. Requirements, as numbered items, each marked must-have or later
5. Roles and permissions
6. Data model and migration impact, based on what you found in the repo and citing file paths
7. Success metrics
8. Risks and open questions
9. Rollout plan

Write each requirement so it can be tested, and give the reason behind it. Don't invent numbers, deadlines, or customer facts. Where I haven't supplied one, write "TBD" and list it under open questions.

Before finishing, have a fresh subagent review the PRD against the sections above. It should flag only gaps that affect correctness or completeness, and should not suggest extra scope. Fix what it finds.

Give me a one-line update before you start the repo search and a short recap at the end, listing the file path, the assumptions you made, and the open questions.

You're done when docs/prd-team-workspaces.md exists with all nine sections filled in and the review gaps are fixed.
